$comment: Array-items part-default case table shared byte-for-byte by the OpenAPI form engines. Each case is rendered as a whole OpenAPI document and derives an array property's emitted media type from its RESOLVED ITEMS DECLARATION on both form lanes. Multipart rendering is <Content-Type>:<body> joined in element order. Outcomes distinguish refusal from missing-required-choice. Corrected 2026-08-26: the superseded typeless-items refusal was removed. Rewritten 2026-09-01 for R4: the urlencoded lane no longer reads application/json off an array CONTAINER. It takes the item-type default the editions' own table names, and where that default defines no serialization for a container -- text/plain for primitive items, application/octet-stream for typeless or artifact-encoded-string items -- the property carries a required `propertyMedia` choice and this table supplies none, so those cells decide missing-required-choice before inspecting a value. Items that resolve to no member at all (a union that does not collapse, a choice supplying no single member) are a different cell that no choice repairs and stay refused. Nested arrays remain refused on multipart, where they have no repeated-part mapping. All other items-derived defaults are unchanged.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|string
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema is a string with no binary signal, so the applicable row is 'for other primitive types - text/plain'. The same edition's multipart guidance states it a second time and directly for arrays: 'If the property is a primitive, or an array of primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain'; 'If the property is complex, or an array of complex values, the default Content-Type is application/json'.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|integer
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema is an integer, so the applicable row is 'for other primitive types - text/plain'. The same edition's multipart guidance states it a second time and directly for arrays: 'If the property is a primitive, or an array of primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain'; 'If the property is complex, or an array of complex values, the default Content-Type is application/json'.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|object
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema is an object, so the applicable row is 'for object - application/json'. The same edition's multipart guidance states it a second time and directly for arrays: 'If the property is a primitive, or an array of primitive values, the default Content-Type is text/plain'; 'If the property is complex, or an array of complex values, the default Content-Type is application/json'.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|nested-array
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema is itself an array, so the row recurses with no base case, and no accepted edition states how the members of an inner array map onto one part name. Deciding that would be authorship rather than incorporation, so the candidate refuses before dispatch (deference order rung 4).

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|unconstrained
cases.basis: The openapi-3.0 family specification §9.3 derives this array part from its resolved items declaration. The items declaration is typeless, has no default concrete part type, and requires configuration.propertyMedia. This table supplies no configuration, so admission remains represented while invocation and the direct write probe reach missing-required-choice before inspecting either supplied value.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|string-base64
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. `contentEncoding` is not a keyword of the 3.0 Schema Object's dialect - the 3.0 binary signal is `format` - so the applicable row is the one for a string with no binary format, and the annotation carries no content-encoding force.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|union-type
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. Every 3.0 edition states of the Schema Object: 'type - Value MUST be a string. Multiple types via an array are not supported.' An array-valued `type` is therefore not a union declaration on this line and no part carriage follows from one.

cases.name: 3.0.3|multipart|union-choice
cases.basis: OAS 3.0.3 Encoding Object, contentType: 'for array - the default is defined based on the inner type'. The items schema declares a choice with more than one non-null branch, which `the openapi family specifications` §9.2 refuses: it declares value-dependent alternatives and leaves no single faithful form carriage.

cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded|string
cases.basis: R4 (ratified 2026-09-01) reads the edition's default-`contentType` table literally: an array property takes THE ITEM-TYPE DEFAULT, not its container's application/json. On multipart that is invisible, because an array property expands into one part per item and each part already carries the item's own declaration. On the content-based urlencoded lane the whole array rides one field, so the selected media type has to define the bytes of the CONTAINER. The items declare a plain string, so the item-type default is text/plain, under which no accepted edition defines the serialization of an array. The family documents' section 9.3 compound-default rule gives that cell no governed wire form and their section 9.3 `propertyMedia` configuration point supplies the remedy: one concrete media type, absent which the invocation refuses before dispatch as the context-required species. Decision: missing-required-choice.

cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded|integer
cases.basis: R4 (ratified 2026-09-01) reads the edition's default-`contentType` table literally: an array property takes THE ITEM-TYPE DEFAULT, not its container's application/json. On multipart that is invisible, because an array property expands into one part per item and each part already carries the item's own declaration. On the content-based urlencoded lane the whole array rides one field, so the selected media type has to define the bytes of the CONTAINER. The items declare integer, a primitive, so the item-type default is text/plain, under which no accepted edition defines the serialization of an array. Same cell and same remedy as the string row. Decision: missing-required-choice.

cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded|object
cases.basis: R4 (ratified 2026-09-01) reads the edition's default-`contentType` table literally: an array property takes THE ITEM-TYPE DEFAULT, not its container's application/json. On multipart that is invisible, because an array property expands into one part per item and each part already carries the item's own declaration. On the content-based urlencoded lane the whole array rides one field, so the selected media type has to define the bytes of the CONTAINER. The items declare an object, whose default row is application/json, and JSON does define the serialization of an array of objects. The container therefore keeps governed bytes and the emission is unchanged by R4 -- this is the one urlencoded row where the item-derived selection and the superseded container-derived selection coincide.

cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded|nested-array
cases.basis: R4 (ratified 2026-09-01) reads the edition's default-`contentType` table literally: an array property takes THE ITEM-TYPE DEFAULT, not its container's application/json. On multipart that is invisible, because an array property expands into one part per item and each part already carries the item's own declaration. On the content-based urlencoded lane the whole array rides one field, so the selected media type has to define the bytes of the CONTAINER. The items are themselves an array, so the item-type default recurses and bottoms out at the inner primitive's text/plain, under which no accepted edition defines the serialization of an array. Decision: missing-required-choice. The multipart sibling refuses instead, because there the nested array has no declaration-defined repeated-part mapping -- a different cell with no stated remedy.

cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded|unconstrained
cases.basis: R4 (ratified 2026-09-01) reads the edition's default-`contentType` table literally: an array property takes THE ITEM-TYPE DEFAULT, not its container's application/json. On multipart that is invisible, because an array property expands into one part per item and each part already carries the item's own declaration. On the content-based urlencoded lane the whole array rides one field, so the selected media type has to define the bytes of the CONTAINER. The items are typeless. On the 3.1 line a typeless declaration defaults to application/octet-stream, which defines no array serialization; on the 3.0 line a typeless resolved declaration has no default concrete type at all. Both land on the same cell the 3.0 document's section 9.3 configuration point names in one sentence -- required "on the content-based form-urlencoded path and for a multipart part alike ... whenever the preceding selection yields no single concrete media type". Decision: missing-required-choice on every accepted edition.

The items declare an artifact-encoded string -- `contentEncoding` on the 3.1 line, `format: byte` on the 3.0 line -- whose default row is application/octet-stream, which defines no array serialization. Decision: missing-required-choice.

cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded|union-type
cases.basis: R4 (ratified 2026-09-01) reads the edition's default-`contentType` table literally: an array property takes THE ITEM-TYPE DEFAULT, not its container's application/json. On multipart that is invisible, because an array property expands into one part per item and each part already carries the item's own declaration. On the content-based urlencoded lane the whole array rides one field, so the selected media type has to define the bytes of the CONTAINER. The items declare a union that does not collapse to one non-null type, so no item-type default resolves at all. Section 5.2 leaves the property with no resolved member declaration, which is not the `propertyMedia` cell: no media choice supplies a member the declaration does not have. cases.name: 3.0.3|urlencoded|union-choice
cases.basis: R4 (ratified 2026-09-01) reads the edition's default-`contentType` table literally: an array property takes THE ITEM-TYPE DEFAULT, not its container's application/json.
